blocks.orig: Katavi National Park is a relatively untouched wilderness. The park is located in the remote area southwest of Tanzania, in an arm of the Rift Valley and ends in the shallow of Lake Rukwa. It lies on a high flood plain surrounding Lake Katavi, south of the Mahale Mountains. The wilderness of Katavi is one of the most virgin areas in the country. Katavi is home to the largest herds of buffalo on the planet.
blocks.html: Katavi National Park is a wilderness that has remained relatively untouched. You will find it in the remote southwest of Tanzania, in an arm of the Rift Valley, where it runs down to the shallows of Lake Rukwa. The park sits on a high flood plain around Lake Katavi, to the south of the Mahale Mountains. Katavi's wilderness counts among the most virgin areas in the country, and it is home to the largest buffalo herds on the planet.

blocks.orig: Katavi’s dramatic landscape is diverse and unique. It contains of flooded areas with thick reeds and dense waterways. And these waterways are home to a huge population of around 200 hippos, crocodiles and different bird life. In the forests to the west, tree tops cover herds of buffalo and elephant. Seasonal lakes fill with dirty colored water after the rains. As a result animals come here from every corner of the park to drink. These include the rare species of roan and sable antelope and a must-see for visitors looking to explore the continent’s wilderness during a private safari. Katavi national park offers excellent game viewing with a real wilderness atmosphere. And therefore fantastic opportunities to take photos!
blocks.html: The landscape of Katavi is dramatic, varied and unique. It is made up of flooded areas with thick reeds and dense waterways, which are home to a large population of around 200 hippos, along with crocodiles and a variety of birds. In the forests to the west, herds of buffalo and elephant move beneath the tree tops. After the rains, seasonal lakes fill up with muddy water, which draws animals from every corner of the park to drink. Among them are the rare roan and sable antelope, a must-see if you want to explore the continent's wilderness on a private safari. Katavi National Park combines excellent game viewing with a genuine wilderness feel, which makes for fantastic photo opportunities!

blocks.orig: This National park offers unspoilt wildlife viewing far off the beaten track! Several large herds of thousands of Cape Buffaloes, an estimated 4000 elephants live in the park. In addition an abundance of zebras, wildebeest, giraffes, eland, sable and roan antelopes can be found roaming in the park. Cheetahs, wild dogs, hyenas, leopards, and lions watch them closely for an opportunity to hunt.
blocks.html: Far off the beaten track, this national park offers wildlife viewing that is still unspoilt! It is home to several large herds of thousands of Cape Buffaloes and to an estimated 4000 elephants. Zebras, wildebeest, giraffes, eland, and sable and roan antelopes also roam the park in abundance, while cheetahs, wild dogs, hyenas, leopards and lions keep a close eye on them, waiting for a chance to hunt.

blocks.orig: The hippos move together closely in any pool of sufficient depth towards the end of the dry season. However, this leads to fights between males during this time. As a result these territorial fights are an almost daily event!
blocks.html: Towards the end of the dry season, the hippos crowd together in any pool that is deep enough. This leads to fights between the males at that time of year, and these territorial clashes happen almost every day!

blocks.orig: Furthermore you can find a large variety of birds living around the shores of the rivers. In total 450 different species live in Katavi National Park.
blocks.html: A wide variety of birds also lives along the riverbanks. Altogether, 450 different species are found in Katavi National Park.

blocks.orig: Mahale national park is located near Katavi, along the shores of Lake Tanganyika, south of Kigoma. It is a famous destination to come face to face with the endangered chimpanzees. Definitely worth to combine it with your trip!
blocks.html: Close to Katavi, on the shores of Lake Tanganyika and south of Kigoma, lies Mahale national park. It is well known as a place to meet the endangered chimpanzees face to face, and it is well worth combining with your trip!

blocks.orig: The location makes the park difficult to accessible by jeep, so a flight is recommended and can be taken from different locations in the country.
blocks.html: Because of its location, the park is hard to reach by jeep, so we recommend flying in; flights leave from various places in the country.

blocks.orig: My name is Michael and I am a guide at Katavi National Park for 12 years. Our guests are always impressed with the huge numbers elephants they can see here. But the hippos are the biggest attraction, especially when the water levels are low and the hippos are fighting for every inch left in the water holes! Some clients spend many hours taking pictures here.
blocks.html: I'm Michael, and I have worked as a guide at Katavi National Park for 12 years. The huge numbers of elephants they see here always impress our guests. Still, the hippos are the main attraction, particularly when the water is low and they fight over every last inch of the water holes! Some guests spend hours here taking photos.

blocks.orig: Which hotel? Katavi Wildlife Camp: It is located in the Katisunga plain. From your vantage point on the veranda of your tent or from the upper viewing lounge, you have a great view of the game and maybe even some hunting from predators!
blocks.html: Where to stay? Katavi Wildlife Camp sits on the Katisunga plain. From the veranda of your tent or the upper viewing lounge you get a great view of the wildlife, and you might even witness predators on the hunt!

blocks.orig: Katavi National Park can be visited all year round. During the months of June to October and December to February, the animals congregate around the remaining water holes and can be reached easily. During the rainy season, the extensive wetlands offer splendid scenery to adventurous visitors.
blocks.html: You can visit Katavi National Park at any time of year. From June to October and from December to February, the animals gather around the water holes that remain and are easy to reach. In the rainy season, the vast wetlands provide splendid scenery for adventurous visitors.

blocks.orig: Katavi national park is a true wilderness, providing the few intrepid travellers who make it there with a thrilling taste of Tanzania as if it must have been a century ago. Home to the largest herds of buffalo on the planet, Katavi National Park is a relatively untouched paradise.
blocks.html: Katavi National Park is real wilderness. The few intrepid travellers who get there enjoy a thrilling taste of Tanzania as it must have been a century ago. With the largest herds of buffalo on the planet, Katavi National Park remains a relatively untouched paradise.
